verdict.rationale: MoQ documents JWT-based authentication and official client libraries for Rust, TypeScript and FFI targets, plus a quick-start demo that starts a relay and opens a player. That is a thin basis for authenticated client connection. There is no documented server-side session-creation API, no flow for minting scoped join tokens, and no short end-to-end walkthrough tying token issuance to SDK connection. missing for 10: server-side session creation, documented scoped token minting (claims/permissions), an end-to-end server-to-client auth flow guide, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: Encrypted via TLS and authenticated via JWT.
Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
The default demo starts a relay, publishes a test video, and opens the web player.
